newsitem.title: USA: Polaroid looking to shore up Russia sales.
newsitem.headline: Polaroid looking to shore up Russia sales.

text.p: Polaroid Corp said Tuesday it is "aggressively" addressing the sales drop it experienced in Russia, which contributed largely to the company's third quarter decline in worldwide sales.
The company said it is addressing the sales drop by doubling the number of distributors and hiring new sales representatives, as well as broadening its marketing in the country.
Polaroid said several other markets, particularly Western Europe and Japan, showed strong retail performances in the quarter.

Worldwide sales overall stood at $298.8 million in the quarter compared to $311.8 million in the same period in 1995. Although Western Europe and Japan markets came in strong, the results were offset by lagging sales in Russia.

Sales in the United States rose to $270.3 million from $268.2 million in the same period the prior year. However, when licensing income was excluded, sales in the U.S. dropped "moderately," the company said.
Polaroid spokesman Robert Guenther declined to release the dollar figure of the drop in U.S. sales.
